sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是NPR的《隐藏大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Amidst the confusion and chaos of the COVID-19 pandemic,
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情带来的困惑与混乱之中，

sentences.en: many of us have sought out a long-trusted lifeline,
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都在寻找一条长期以来值得信赖的生命线，

sentences.en: Reporters venturing out to hospitals, to remote areas, to nursing homes,
sentences.zh: 记者们深入医院、偏远地区和养老院，

sentences.en: they tell us what's happening in the world, in our country,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们世界上、我们国家里，
以及我们社区中正在发生什么。

sentences.en: They let us track the spread of disease,
sentences.zh: 他们让我们能够追踪疾病的传播，

sentences.en: the availability of ICU beds, the well-being of our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 了解重症监护室床位的可用情况，以及邻居们的健康状况。

sentences.en: It should come as no surprise that in the past couple of months,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，在过去的几个月里，

sentences.en: print and online local newspaper readership has soared.
sentences.zh: 当地报纸的纸质版和网络版读者人数激增。

sentences.en: Yet at this time, when the value of local journalism is most evident,
sentences.zh: 然而，在当地新闻价值最显而易见的当下，

sentences.en: as readers are inhaling article after article,
sentences.zh: 当读者们如饥似渴地阅读着一篇又一篇报道时，
报社却并没有蒸蒸日上。

sentences.en: Well, it is a difficult day for journalism in Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 对于克利夫兰的新闻业来说，这是艰难的一天。

sentences.en: Today, the Plain Dealer newsroom went from 38 employees down to 16.
sentences.zh: 今天，《平原经销商报》的新闻编辑部员工从38人裁减到了16人。

sentences.en: Well, North Dakota's two largest newspapers are taking steps to trim costs
sentences.zh: 北达科他州最大的两家报纸正在采取措施削减成本，
以应对新冠疫情的爆发。
新冠疫情让报社的广告业务化为乌有。

sentences.en: The 98 of the company's 375 employees have been furloughed
sentences.zh: 公司375名员工中有98人被强制休假，

sentences.en: or had their hours cut back.
The problem is only going to grow.
sentences.zh: 这个问题只会愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: Advertising revenue, which newspapers rely on,
sentences.zh: 报纸所依赖的广告收入，
和人们保持社交距离而正在消失。

sentences.en: COVID-19 might be the final nail in the coffin.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情可能是压死骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: the financial health of many newspapers has been precarious
sentences.zh: 许多报纸的财务状况一直岌岌可危，

sentences.en: in good economic times and bad.
sentences.zh: 无论经济形势好坏皆是如此。

sentences.en: If you talk to people who don't subscribe to their local paper,

sentences.en: you can see why the industry is in dire straits.
sentences.zh: 你就能明白为什么这个行业正处于水深火热之中。

sentences.en: Here are some Denver residents we spoke with.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们采访的一些丹佛居民。

sentences.en: Uh, I've never subscribed to a local publication.
sentences.zh: 呃，我从来没订阅过当地的出版物。

sentences.en: I usually just get the free ones, like, Westward.
sentences.zh: 我通常只拿免费的，比如《Westward》。

sentences.en: The free one that comes out in the little red bins all over Denver.

sentences.en: That's what I wanted the paper for, is the coupons.

Their logic, and that of millions of Americans,

sentences.zh: 有很多选择可以让你花很少甚至不用钱就能读到新闻。

Why subscribe if you don't have time to read the paper?

sentences.en: If you want to save money?

sentences.en: That's because newspapers are not like most things we buy.
sentences.zh: 这是因为报纸不像我们购买的大多数商品。

sentences.en: If we decide not to buy an espresso machine, we save money.
sentences.zh: 如果我们决定不买浓缩咖啡机，我们就能省钱。

sentences.en: But if we decide not to pay for a police department,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们决定不为警察局买单，

sentences.en: we might save money in the short run,
sentences.zh: 短期内我们可能省了钱，

sentences.en: but end up paying much more in the long run.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，最终付出的代价会大得多。

sentences.en: Most of us treat newspapers like consumer products,
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人把报纸当作消费品来对待，

sentences.en: but new research suggests they might be more like police departments.
sentences.zh: 但最新研究表明，它们可能更像警察局。
